status: PILOT — proposed by the team, not an instructor requirement
notes: Sample size is deliberately small. Per the breakdown's sample-size rule, the
final count is decided after a pilot run exposes instrumentation problems, not
chosen up front. These cases exist to prove the harness works end to end.
max_tool_calls is set from core._MAX_AGENT_STEPS = 3 (the real code constant),
not copied from a lecture example.
Cases marked requires_ledger_fixture depend on evaluation/fixtures/seed_finance.py.
expected_answer_contains is intentionally empty on every case: filling it in
requires a frozen ledger AND a recorded run, and inventing expected strings
before measuring would be fabricating ground truth.

cases.input: How much did I spend in total?
cases.notes: Aggregate numeric question -> SQL route. The clearest routing signal.

cases.input: What is my largest single expense?
Which receipt has cooking oil on it?
What did I buy at SM Supermarket?
What was on my recent receipt?
cases.notes: Ambiguous 'recent receipt' with >1 receipt in the ledger must trigger the pre-loop clarification and call NO tool. This is the deterministic disambiguation path (core._RECENT_RECEIPT_RE), so it should pass without a model reaching the loop.

cases.input: What is the capital of France?
cases.notes: Out-of-scope question. The agent must terminate cleanly rather than loop or crash; whether it answers or declines is recorded, not asserted, until the team agrees the desired behaviour.

cases.input: How much did I spend at 7-Eleven?
cases.notes: Genuinely answerable either way (vendor + amount). Route is recorded, not asserted — this measures loop/termination behaviour, not routing.
